correctness.rationale: For unsigned incidence N, NN^T=Q(G), N^TN=A(LG)+2I. G is connected nonbipartite (contains an odd cycle), so N has full row rank; m-n=t-1 gives exactly t-1 additional eigenvalues -2. For adjoining a length (2h+1) cycle at one cut vertex, the 2h fresh vertices form even path matrix B with inertia (h,0,h), determinant (-1)^h and b^TB^-1b=2(-1)^(h-1). Its Schur complement in M=Q-2I is M if li≡3 mod4, or M+4ee^T if li≡1 mod4. The inverse terminal diagonal g remains -1/2 until first 1(mod4) block then g=1/(4q-2), giving nonzero Schur multipliers and at most one sign flip. The consequent inertias and determinant telescoping yield the two exact formulas independent of attachment position. Independently built 10 odd-cycle chains of lengths 3,5,7 with up to four blocks and varied attachments; exact SymPy integer determinants matched and independently evaluated real symmetric eigenvalue signs matched with no near-zero eigenvalues. Finite examples corroborate but do not prove the unbounded induction.

Francis–Uptain 2026 concerns bridge-connected gadgets and unbounded positive signature, not vertex-glued blocks. New exact boundary-resolvent telescoping extends this known method to a naturally different infinite topology; t<=2 cases are credited.
